HOS.1.1.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and of Jeroboam son of Jehoash, king of Israel.

notes.text: Hebrew Joash, a variant of Jehoash

HOS.1.2.text: When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, He told him, “Go, take a prostitute as your wife and have children of adultery, because this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD.”

HOS.1.3.text: So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

HOS.1.4.text: Then the LORD said to Hosea, “Name him Jezreel, for soon I will bring the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.

notes.text: Jezreel means God sows; also in verse 11.

HOS.1.5.text: And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel.”

HOS.1.6.text: Gomer again conceived and gave birth to a daughter, and the LORD said to Hosea, “Name her Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should ever forgive them.

notes.text: Lo-ruhamah means she has not received mercy.

HOS.1.7.text: Yet I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them—not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God.”

HOS.1.8.text: After she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, Gomer conceived and gave birth to a son.

HOS.1.9.text: And the LORD said, “Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God.

notes.text: Lo-ammi means not My people.
Hebrew I am not yours

HOS.1.10.text: Yet the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. And it will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’

notes.text: Cited in Romans 9:26

HOS.1.11.text: Then the people of Judah and of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint for themselves one leader, and will go up out of the land. For great will be the day of Jezreel.

notes.text: Hebrew Ammi

HOS.2.1.text: and of your sisters, ‘My loved one.’

notes.text: Or Mercy is shown; Hebrew Ruhamah, which means she has received mercy

HOS.2.2.text: for she is not My wife,
and I am not her husband.
Let her remove the adultery from her face
and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.

HOS.2.3.text: Otherwise, I will strip her naked
and expose her like the day of her birth.
I will make her like a desert
and turn her into a parched land,
and I will let her die of thirst.

HOS.2.4.text: I will have no compassion on her children,
because they are the children of adultery.

HOS.2.5.text: For their mother has played the harlot
and has conceived them in disgrace.
who give me bread and water,
wool and linen, oil and drink.’

HOS.2.6.text: I will hedge up her path with thorns;

notes.text: Hebrew your path

HOS.2.6.text: I will enclose her with a wall,
so she cannot find her way.

HOS.2.7.text: She will pursue her lovers but not catch them;
she will seek them but not find them.
‘I will return to my first husband,
for then I was better off than now.’

HOS.2.8.text: that it was I who gave her grain,
who lavished on her silver and gold—

HOS.2.9.text: Therefore I will take back My grain in its time
and My new wine in its season;
I will take away My wool and linen,
which were given to cover her nakedness.

HOS.2.10.text: And then I will expose her lewdness
in the sight of her lovers,
and no one will deliver her

HOS.2.11.text: I will put an end to all her exultation:
her feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths—

HOS.2.12.text: I will destroy her vines and fig trees,
which she thinks are the wages paid by her lovers.
So I will make them into a thicket,
and the beasts of the field will devour them.

HOS.2.13.text: I will punish her for the days of the Baals
when she burned incense to them,
when she decked herself with rings and jewelry,

HOS.2.14.text: and lead her to the wilderness,

HOS.2.15.text: There I will give back her vineyards
and make the Valley of Achor

notes.text: Achor means trouble.

HOS.2.15.text: There she will respond as she did
in the days of her youth,
as in the day she came up out of Egypt.

notes.text: Hebrew my Ishi

HOS.2.16.text: and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’

notes.text: Hebrew my Baal

HOS.2.17.text: For I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals;
no longer will their names be invoked.

HOS.2.18.text: On that day I will make a covenant for them
with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air
and the creatures that crawl on the ground.
And I will abolish bow and sword
and weapons of war in the land,
and will make them lie down in safety.

HOS.2.19.text: So I will betroth you to Me forever;
I will betroth you in righteousness and justice,

notes.text: Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

HOS.2.20.text: And I will betroth you in faithfulness,
and you will know the LORD.”

HOS.2.21.text: and they will respond to the earth.

HOS.2.22.text: And the earth will respond to the grain,
to the new wine and oil,
and they will respond to Jezreel.

notes.text: Jezreel means God sows.

HOS.2.23.text: And I will sow her as My own in the land,
and I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’

notes.text: Hebrew Lo-ruhamah; LXX I will love her who was not loved

HOS.2.23.text: I will say to those called ‘Not My People,’

notes.text: Hebrew Lo-ammi
Cited in Romans 9:25 and 1 Peter 2:10

HOS.3.1.text: Then the LORD said to me, “Go show love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and offer raisin cakes to idols.”

notes.text: Or Go show love to a woman who is loved by another
Literally and love raisin cakes

HOS.3.2.text: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.

notes.text: 15 shekels is approximately 6 ounces or 171 grams of silver.
Or a homer and a half of barley; that is, a total of approximately 9.36 bushels or 330 liters (probably about 436 pounds or 198 kilograms of barley); LXX a homer of barley and a wineskin full of wine

HOS.3.3.text: Then I said to her, “You must live with me for many days; you must not be promiscuous or belong to another, and I will do the same for you.”

HOS.3.4.text: For the Israelites must live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or idol.

HOS.3.5.text: Afterward, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days.

HOS.4.1.text: Hear the word of the LORD,
for the LORD has a case
against the people of the land:
“There is no truth, no loving devotion,
and no knowledge of God in the land!

HOS.4.2.text: one act of bloodshed follows another.

HOS.4.3.text: and all who dwell in it will waste away
with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air;
even the fish of the sea disappear.

HOS.4.4.text: for your people are like those

notes.text: Or for My case is against you, O priests

HOS.4.5.text: and the prophet will stumble with you by night;
so I will destroy your mother—

HOS.4.6.text: I will also reject you as My priests.
Since you have forgotten the law of your God,
I will also forget your children.

HOS.4.7.text: the more they sinned against Me;

notes.text: Or they exchanged their glorious God (Syriac); MT I will exchange their glory

HOS.4.8.text: They feed on the sins of My people

notes.text: Or the sin offerings

HOS.4.8.text: and set their hearts on iniquity.

HOS.4.9.text: I will punish both of them for their ways
and repay them for their deeds.

HOS.4.10.text: They will eat but not be satisfied;
they will be promiscuous but not multiply.
For they have stopped obeying the LORD.

HOS.4.12.text: My people consult their wooden idols,
and their divining rods inform them.
For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray
and they have played the harlot against their God.

HOS.4.13.text: and burn offerings on the hills,
And so your daughters turn to prostitution

HOS.4.14.text: I will not punish your daughters
For the men themselves go off with prostitutes
and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes.

HOS.4.15.text: Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel,
do not go up to Beth-aven,

notes.text: Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29.

HOS.4.15.text: and do not swear on oath,

HOS.4.16.text: Can the LORD now shepherd them
like lambs in an open meadow?

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel
Hebrew her shields

HOS.4.19.text: The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings,

notes.text: Hebrew has wrapped her

HOS.4.19.text: and their sacrifices will bring them shame.

HOS.5.1.text: Take heed, O house of Israel!
For this judgment is against you
because you have been a snare at Mizpah,
a net spread out on Tabor.

HOS.5.2.text: The rebels are deep in slaughter;
but I will chastise them all.

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, and 14

HOS.5.3.text: and Israel is not hidden from Me.

HOS.5.4.text: Their deeds do not permit them
for a spirit of prostitution is within them,
and they do not know the LORD.

HOS.5.5.text: Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity;

HOS.5.6.text: They go with their flocks and herds
but they do not find Him;
He has withdrawn Himself from them.

HOS.5.7.text: They have been unfaithful to the LORD;
for they have borne illegitimate children.
Now the New Moon will devour them

notes.text: Or their New Moon feast or the coming month

HOS.5.8.text: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah,
raise the battle cry in Beth-aven:

notes.text: Beth-aven means house of wickedness. This is a derogatory term for Bethel, which means house of God; see 1 Kings 12:28–29.

HOS.5.10.text: are like those who move boundary stones;

notes.text: See Proverbs 22:28 and Proverbs 23:10.

HOS.5.10.text: I will pour out My fury

HOS.5.11.text: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment,
for he is determined to follow worthless idols.

notes.text: Or to follow human precepts

HOS.5.12.text: So I am like a moth to Ephraim,
and like decay to the house of Judah.

HOS.5.13.text: and sent to the great king.

notes.text: Or to King Jareb

HOS.5.14.text: For I am like a lion to Ephraim
and like a young lion to the house of Judah.
I, even I, will tear them to pieces
where no one can rescue them.

HOS.5.15.text: Then I will return to My place
until they admit their guilt and seek My face;
in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”

HOS.6.1.text: Come, let us return to the LORD.
For He has torn us to pieces,
but He will bind up our wounds.

HOS.6.2.text: After two days He will revive us;
on the third day He will raise us up,
that we may live in His presence.

HOS.6.3.text: let us press on to know the LORD.
As surely as the sun rises,
He will come to us like the rain,
like the spring showers that water the earth.

HOS.6.4.text: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim ?

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 10

HOS.6.4.text: What shall I do with you, O Judah?
For your loyalty is like a morning mist,
like the early dew that vanishes.

HOS.6.5.text: Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets;
I have slain them by the words of My mouth,
and My judgments go forth like lightning.

HOS.6.6.text: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice,

notes.text: Cited in Matthew 9:13 and Matthew 12:7

HOS.6.7.text: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant;

notes.text: Or As at Adam, they have transgressed

HOS.6.7.text: there they were unfaithful to Me.

HOS.6.8.text: Gilead is a city of evildoers,

HOS.6.9.text: Like raiders who lie in ambush,
so does a band of priests;
they murder on the way to Shechem;

HOS.6.10.text: I have seen a horrible thing:

notes.text: Or restore the fortunes of My people

HOS.7.1.text: the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed,

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8 and 11

HOS.7.1.text: as well as the crimes of Samaria.
For they practice deceit and thieves break in;

HOS.7.2.text: But they fail to consider in their hearts
that I remember all their evil.
Now their deeds are all around them;

HOS.7.3.text: They delight the king with their evil,
and the princes with their lies.

HOS.7.4.text: like an oven heated by a baker
who needs not stoke the fire
from the kneading to the rising of the dough.

HOS.7.5.text: The princes are inflamed with wine
on the day of our king;

HOS.7.6.text: For they prepare their heart like an oven

notes.text: Literally their baker sleeps

HOS.7.6.text: in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.

HOS.7.7.text: All of them are hot as an oven,
not one of them calls upon Me.

HOS.7.9.text: Even his hair is streaked with gray,

HOS.7.10.text: yet they do not return to the LORD their God;
despite all this, they do not seek Him.

HOS.7.11.text: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove—
calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.

HOS.7.12.text: As they go, I will spread My net over them;
I will bring them down like birds of the air.
when I hear them flocking together.

notes.text: Or I will chastise them according to what was reported against them in the assembly.

HOS.7.13.text: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me!
Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me!

HOS.7.14.text: They do not cry out to Me from their hearts
when they wail upon their beds.
They slash themselves for grain and new wine,

notes.text: Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX; see 1 Kings 18:28. Most Hebrew manuscripts They gather together

HOS.7.15.text: Although I trained and strengthened their arms,

HOS.7.16.text: They turn, but not to the Most High;
they are like a faulty bow.
Their leaders will fall by the sword
for the cursing of their tongue;
for this they will be ridiculed

HOS.8.1.text: Put the ram’s horn to your lips!
An eagle looms over the house of the LORD,
because the people have transgressed My covenant

HOS.8.4.text: They set up kings, but not by Me.
They make princes, but without My approval.
With their silver and gold they make themselves idols,

HOS.8.5.text: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria.

notes.text: Or calf idol; see 1 Kings 12:29.

HOS.8.6.text: For this thing is from Israel—
a craftsman made it, and it is not God.
It will be broken to pieces,

HOS.8.7.text: and they shall reap the whirlwind.
what sprouts fails to yield flour.
the foreigners would swallow it up.

HOS.8.8.text: Now they are among the nations

HOS.8.9.text: For they have gone up to Assyria
like a wild donkey on its own.

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 11

HOS.8.10.text: Though they hire allies among the nations,
I will now round them up,
and they will begin to diminish
under the oppression of the king of princes.

HOS.8.11.text: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin,
they became his altars for sinning.

HOS.8.12.text: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law,
they regarded them as something strange.

HOS.8.13.text: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me,
and though they eat the meat,
the LORD does not accept them.
Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins:

HOS.8.14.text: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces;
Judah has multiplied its fortified cities.
But I will send fire upon their cities,
and it will consume their citadels.

HOS.9.1.text: for you have played the harlot against your God;
you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.

HOS.9.2.text: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them,
and the new wine will fail them.

HOS.9.3.text: in the land of the LORD;

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; similarly in verses 8, 11, 13, and 16

HOS.9.3.text: and eat unclean food in Assyria.

HOS.9.4.text: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD,
and their sacrifices will not please Him,
but will be to them like the bread of mourners;
all who eat will be defiled.
For their bread will be for themselves;
it will not enter the house of the LORD.

HOS.9.5.text: What will you do on the appointed day,
on the day of the LORD’s feast?

HOS.9.6.text: For even if they flee destruction,
Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles,
and thorns will overrun their tents.

HOS.9.7.text: The days of punishment have come;
the days of retribution have arrived—
The prophet is called a fool,

notes.text: Or The prophet is the watchman over Ephraim, the people of my God

HOS.9.8.text: yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths.
Hostility is in the house of his God!

HOS.9.9.text: as in the days of Gibeah;

HOS.9.10.text: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.
I saw your fathers as the firstfruits
of the fig tree in its first season.

HOS.9.11.text: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird,
with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.

HOS.9.12.text: Even if they raise their children,
I will bereave them of each one.
when I turn away from them!

HOS.9.13.text: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre,

HOS.9.15.text: All their evil appears at Gilgal,
I will drive them from My house
for the wickedness of their deeds.
I will no longer love them;

HOS.9.16.text: I will slay the darlings of their wombs.

HOS.9.17.text: because they have not obeyed Him;

HOS.10.1.text: the more he increased the altars.
the better he made the sacred pillars.

HOS.10.2.text: now they must bear their guilt.
The LORD will break down their altars

What can a king do for us?”

like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.

HOS.10.5.text: The people of Samaria will fear

HOS.10.5.text: those who rejoiced in its glory—
for it has been taken from them into exile.

HOS.10.6.text: Yes, it will be carried to Assyria

notes.text: Or to King Jareb

HOS.10.6.text: Ephraim will be seized with shame;

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 11

HOS.10.6.text: Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.

notes.text: Or of its own counsel

HOS.10.7.text: Samaria will be carried off with her king
like a twig on the surface of the water.

HOS.10.8.text: The high places of Aven will be destroyed—

notes.text: Or of wickedness; Aven is a reference to Beth-aven (a derogatory term for Bethel); see verse 5.

HOS.10.8.text: it is the sin of Israel;
thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars.
Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!”
and to the hills, “Fall on us!”

notes.text: Cited in Luke 23:30; see also Revelation 6:16.

HOS.10.9.text: Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel,
Did not the battle in Gibeah

notes.text: Or Did not the battle overtake the sons of iniquity in Gibeah?

HOS.10.10.text: I will chasten them when I please;
nations will be gathered against them

HOS.10.11.text: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh;
but I will place a yoke on her fair neck.
I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow,
and Jacob will break the hard ground.

HOS.10.12.text: and reap the fruit of loving devotion;
For it is time to seek the LORD
until He comes and sends righteousness

HOS.10.13.text: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice;
you have eaten the fruit of lies.
Because you have trusted in your own way
and in the multitude of your mighty men,

HOS.10.14.text: the roar of battle will rise against your people,
so that all your fortresses will be demolished
when mothers were dashed to pieces

HOS.10.15.text: Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel,
the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.

HOS.11.1.text: When Israel was a child, I loved him,
and out of Egypt I called My son.

notes.text: Cited in Matthew 2:15

HOS.11.2.text: But the more I called Israel,
the farther they departed from Me.

notes.text: LXX; Hebrew The more they called them, the more they went from them.

HOS.11.2.text: and burned incense to carved images.

HOS.11.3.text: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk,

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8, 9, and 12

HOS.11.5.text: Will they not return to the land of Egypt

HOS.11.7.text: My people are bent on turning from Me.
Though they call to the Most High,
He will by no means exalt them.

HOS.11.8.text: How could I give you up, O Ephraim?
How could I surrender you, O Israel?
How could I make you like Admah?
How could I treat you like Zeboiim?
My heart is turned within Me;

HOS.11.9.text: I will not execute the full fury of My anger;
I will not turn back to destroy Ephraim.
For I am God and not man—
and I will not come in wrath.

HOS.11.10.text: They will walk after the LORD;
He will roar like a lion.
His children will come trembling from the west.

HOS.11.11.text: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt
and like doves from the land of Assyria.
Then I will settle them in their homes,

HOS.11.12.text: the house of Israel with deceit;

notes.text: Or and Judah is unruly against God, the faithful Holy One
That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verses 8 and 14

HOS.12.1.text: and pursues the east wind all day long;

He will punish Jacob according to his ways

notes.text: That is, northwest Mesopotamia

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel; also in verse 12

HOS.13.1.text: But he incurred guilt through Baal,

idols skillfully made from their silver,
all of them the work of craftsmen.

HOS.13.3.text: Therefore they will be like the morning mist,
like the early dew that vanishes,
like chaff blown from a threshing floor,
like smoke through an open window.

HOS.13.4.text: Yet I am the LORD your God
ever since the land of Egypt;
you know no God but Me,

HOS.13.14.text: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol;
I will redeem them from Death.

notes.text: Or Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol? Shall I redeem them from Death?

HOS.13.14.text: Where, O Death, are your plagues?
Where, O Sheol, is your sting?

notes.text: LXX Where, O Death, is your penalty? Where, O Hades, is your sting? Cited in 1 Corinthians 15:55

HOS.13.14.text: Compassion is hidden from My eyes.

HOS.13.15.text: Although he flourishes among his brothers,
and his spring will run dry.
The wind will plunder his treasury

HOS.13.16.text: because she has rebelled against her God.
They will fall by the sword;
their little ones will be dashed to pieces,
and their pregnant women ripped open.

HOS.14.1.text: Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God,
for you have stumbled by your iniquity.

HOS.14.2.text: Say to Him: “Take away all our iniquity

notes.text: LXX and Syriac; Hebrew that we may present our lips as sacrificial bulls

HOS.14.3.text: nor will we ride on horses.
We will never again say, ‘Our gods!’
to the work of our own hands.
For in You the fatherless find compassion.”

HOS.14.4.text: for My anger has turned away from them.

HOS.14.5.text: I will be like the dew to Israel;
he will blossom like the lily
and take root like the cedars of Lebanon.

HOS.14.6.text: and his splendor will be like the olive tree,
his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon.

HOS.14.7.text: They will return and dwell in his shade;
they will grow grain and blossom like the vine.
His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.

HOS.14.8.text: O Ephraim, what have I to do

notes.text: That is, the northern kingdom of Israel

HOS.14.8.text: It is I who answer and watch over him.
I am like a flourishing cypress;

notes.text: Or pine or juniper or fir

HOS.14.9.text: Whoever is wise, let him understand these things;
whoever is discerning, let him know them.
For the ways of the LORD are right,
and the righteous walk in them
but the rebellious stumble in them.
